text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 1.2% today as oil prices and refinery demand tightened. U.S. crude rose to $83.90 per barrel following geopolitical tensions—Iran's retaliation against U.S. military bases in Jordan and Trump's threat of escalation pushed prices higher. Refineries are running at 97.4% capacity, near maximum levels, which boosts margins for a refiner like MPC: when oil costs more but you're already running flat-out, you can pass costs to customers while squeezing more profit per barrel processed.

The two-week rally reflects a shift in the oil market's fundamentals. Gasoline and diesel inventories remain tight (206.8 million and 103.4 million barrels respectively), and geopolitical risks now outweigh the longer-term supply boost from new Venezuelan production agreements announced this week—those deals take time to ramp, so near-term supply pressure stays real.
